evidence.summary: Arjun Nair filed a complaint against Rohan Malhotra for unauthorized bank transfers totaling Rs. 45,00,000 between January and April 2024. The purpose was to deliver vehicles and manage a Whitefield warehouse. The case involves financial disputes related to excise duties and tax assessments.
Kaveri Auto Traders is accused of fabricating six vehicle invoices. The prosecution disputes their authenticity, citing forensic examination findings. The case involves excise duty and tax disputes.

The case involves a transaction summary from a fictional courtroom script, listing financial transactions involving a personal vehicle loan and an online rummy/betting wallet. The accused is accused of misusing funds from these transactions.

Kaveri Auto Traders is facing a financial dispute related to GST verification. The company's address on invoices does not match the registered GSTIN in departmental records, indicating a potential issue with the authenticity of the GST registration. This case falls under the Excise/Tax category due to the involvement of GST, and it is classified as Financial because it pertains to financial matters.

Kaveri Auto Traders is accused of fabricating six invoices attributed to them. The case involves financial disputes related to excise duties and GST, as the invoices were retrospectively dated and used in a courtroom script to support the fabricated claim.

STATE, on the complaint of ARJUN NAIR, seeks to hold ROHAN MALHOTRA liable for breach of a partnership agreement. The dispute centers around disputed invoices and bank transfer receipts. The case raises questions under Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty) and Article 14 (equality before law). The relief sought is for the enforcement of the partnership agreement and payment of dues.
